h1:
Nakhon Ratchasima Zoo (Korat Zoo)
An Open Zoo Where Kids Ride the Tram Through a Safari Zone
intro: Nakhon Ratchasima Zoo, known to locals simply as Korat Zoo, is a large open-style zoo where parents can happily spend the whole day with the kids. Children ride the tram into the safari zone to see giraffes and zebras up close, hold out food for the giraffes and hippos, then finish the day cooling off in the water park. It's a popular family outing in Korat that kids are happy to come back to again and again.
chips: 🦒 Feed the giraffes in the safari zone
🚋 Tour the whole zoo by tram
🏊 A water park for the kids

blocks.html: Nakhon Ratchasima Zoo sits on the Ratchasima–Pak Thong Chai road (Route 304), about 20 kilometres from Korat city. It's one of Thailand's larger zoos, laid out as an open park where the animals live in wide, spacious enclosures rather than small cages. Inside you'll find walking trails past the animals, a savanna-style safari zone, feeding stations, a reptile and aquatic house, and a small water park — enough to keep a family busy from morning into the afternoon.

What makes kids love this place is that they get to do more than just look. Korat Zoo has spots where you can hand-feed the giraffes and hippos, trams and golf carts to ride around the grounds, and a small water park to cool off in — so children come away having learned a bit about animals and burned off some energy too.

items: Safari zone — ride the tram into the open savanna to see giraffes, zebras, deer and other hoofed animals grazing right beside you; usually the part kids get most excited about.
Animal-feeding stations — feed the giraffes and hippos, and feed the flamingos too; food is sold inside, and children can hold it out themselves for an up-close moment.
Tram, golf-cart and bicycle rental — the grounds are big, so take the guided tram or rent a golf cart to drive yourself and spare little legs a long walk.
Children's zoo and reptile house — a small-animal corner to see up close, plus a reptile and aquatic building where kids love watching the fish and snakes.
Water park — a small water park to cool off in; bring swimwear and a towel so the kids can have a proper splash.

Animal shows — there are animal-ability shows such as otters and seals twice a day (around 11 a.m. and 2 p.m.), an activity some families choose to watch and others skip, whichever they're comfortable with.

blocks.title: When to go with kids, and what to bring
blocks.html: Mornings just after opening are best — it's cooler and the animals are more active. Korat gets hot in the middle of the day, so bring a hat, water and sunscreen, plus swimwear if you plan to use the water park. If you have toddlers or older family members along, renting one golf cart makes the day far more comfortable than walking it all.

items: Opening hours — open daily, roughly 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (some periods close around 4 p.m.). Check the zoo's page for the latest times before you go.

Approximate entry fees — around 130 THB for Thai adults and about 40 THB for children aged 3–12; under-3s are free, and it's roughly another 50 THB to bring a car in. Foreign visitors are charged more (prices are approximate and may change).

Getting there — it's on the Ratchasima–Pak Thong Chai road (Route 304), about 20 kilometres from Korat city, a 20–30 minute drive with plenty of parking; you can also take a songthaew or hire a car from town.
Good for which ages — fine for all ages, but especially fun for animal-mad kids aged 3–10; the paths are flat enough for a stroller, and the tram and golf carts help reach the farther zones.

blocks.title: Getting the most out of it, comfortably
blocks.html: Plan for a half to full day, since the grounds are large with several zones, and keep an eye mainly on the heat — take regular water breaks. If you're not comfortable with animal shows, you can skip the show times and focus on the safari zone and the feeding stations, where the animals are out in wide open enclosures — that's really the heart of a visit here anyway.

faq.q: What time does Nakhon Ratchasima Zoo open?
faq.a: It's open daily, roughly 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (some periods close around 4 p.m.). Animal shows usually run twice a day, at about 11 a.m. and 2 p.m. Check the zoo's page for the latest times before you travel.

faq.q: How much is the entry fee for Korat Zoo?
faq.a: Around 130 THB for Thai adults and about 40 THB for children aged 3–12, with under-3s free, plus roughly 50 THB to bring a car in. Foreign visitors are charged more. Prices are approximate, so check again on site.

faq.q: Is it manageable with young children, and what should I bring?
faq.a: It's very manageable — the paths are flat enough for a stroller, and you can rent a tram seat or a golf cart so you're not walking the whole way. Bring a hat, water, sunscreen and swimwear if the kids will use the water park; mornings are cooler.

faq.q: Are there animal-feeding stations and animal shows?
faq.a: Yes — there are feeding spots for giraffes, hippos and flamingos that kids love, and animal-ability shows with otters and seals twice a day that you can watch or skip, whichever you prefer. The real draw here is that the animals live in wide open enclosures and a safari zone you tour by tram.
